To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the frequency and amplitude of spontaneously occurring EPSCs in rat moss cells are increased in the presence of depolarizing stimuli.
depolarization of single neurones in the rat dentate gyrus induces a transient potentiation of the spontaneous EPSPs that are normally observed in neighbouring mossy cells.
depolarization of one dentate granule cell can induce a long lasting potentiation of the amplitude and frequency of its own and other granule cell synaptic inputs to a mossy cell.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms of synaptic plasticity in the dentate gyruse.
the mechanisms underlying the expression of long‐lasting potentiation of spontaneous synaptic transmission in the hippocampus.
